prompt_used:
A solid sculpted bust of the subject carved entirely from graphite — soft pencil-lead grey with a burnished sheen, the surface worked in visible pencil strokes that wrap the form: crosshatching in the recesses, broad shading across the planes, edges softly smudged. Eyes and lips are graphite. Hair keeps its real length and silhouette in long directional strokes. No skin, no real hair. The garment carries through in the same material. Frame from mid-chest to the top of the head. The subject faces us naturally, head upright, with both eyes clearly visible. A real object standing in real light, casting its own shadow. Likeness is critical. Keep permanent structure: lines, scars and the natural asymmetry of the face. Never reshape, enlarge eyes, correct asymmetry or de-age. No held objects — no cups, glasses, phones, books, tools, watches or eyewear. Worn jewellery is fine: necklaces, earrings, piercings. Likeness is essential. maintain expression, micro gestures, imperfections. do not introduce body imperfections. Do not modify body or head shape.
Do not change the hairline, shape or style.
Do not lighten or darken the hair color
Set in a **beautiful old-world artist's atelier**, heavily blurred: aged timber, plaster walls, antique easels, stacked canvases, pinned charcoal studies and drawing tools beneath a huge ribbed iron-and-glass skylight. Soft directional daylight reveals charcoal texture, chalk buildup and airborne dust. Atmospheric, romantic, shallow depth of field.
